lines.text: You're matching each other's pace without thinking about it. That's a squad.
Nobody's looked back to check on the others for an hour. You don't need to. Good.
Keep this rhythm. A squad that walks well together fights well together.
Decent pace. Close the gap at the back, though. Three paces, not ten.
You're doing fine. Talk to each other more. Silence isn't always discipline.
Steady is good. Steady gets us there. Steady and awake is better.
You're strung out like washing on a line. Close up. Now.
Whatever's bothering you two, leave it at the milestone. Pick it up later if you must.
A squad that won't walk together won't stand together. Think about that for the next mile.
Enough. We stop here until you can walk side by side without sulking.
I don't need you to like each other. I need you to trust each other's backs. Today you don't.
If the road were watched right now, we'd be three easy targets. Fix it.
I like this. Just walking. Not even talking. It's nice.
Your turn to pick the song. No, a good one this time.
I'd walk anywhere with this squad. Even the long way.
Pass the water? Thanks. Your turn next stop.
Not bad so far. My feet only hate me a little.
Want to swap who carries the heavy pack? Fair's fair.
Can we not talk for a bit? I'm just tired. It's not you. Mostly.
You're walking too fast. Or I'm walking too slow. Whatever.
Fine, I'll carry it. I always carry it.
I'll walk at the back. You two clearly don't need me up front.
Don't. I'm not in the mood. Just walk.
I'm only here because the mission says so. Let's be clear.
You all move like one creature. It's quite something to watch.
I feel very safe with you. You look out for each other, I can tell.
Is this what a good squad is like? I see why the Leaf is proud.
You seem to know what you're doing. That's reassuring.
Quiet lot, aren't you? I don't mind. Quiet is calm.
A good pace. Not too fast for my old knees.
Is everything all right? You keep looking at each other.
I hope you won't mind me saying, but you seem a little out of sorts today.
Should I walk in the middle? You're rather spread out.
Forgive me, but are you three quarrelling? It's making me nervous.
I'd feel safer if you were speaking to each other.
I didn't pay for an argument. I paid for an escort.
You set the camp up without me saying a word. I could get used to that.
This is a good squad. I don't say it to flatter. Get some sleep.
You took the hard watch without being asked. Noted. Appreciated.
Camp's sound. Fire's low. Good. Eat and rest.
Decent day's work. Tomorrow, a bit more talking on the road.
Watches as I said. Nobody skips. Nobody grumbles. Thank you.
Sit down, all of you. We're going to talk about today. Calmly.
You're tired, and tired makes people sharp. Sleep it off before you say something.
Eat together. Not three corners of the fire. Together.
Nobody sleeps until this is settled. I mean it. Talk.
I've seen squads break over less. Not mine. Not tonight.
Whatever's between you, it's riding along on every step. Put it down.
I'm glad it's you two I'm out here with. Really glad.
Remember this. When we're old and grey and Jonin, remember this fire.
Let's save the last rice ball and split it three ways. Squad rules.
Good day, all things considered. Tomorrow will be better.
Wake me for second watch. Actually wake me, don't just poke me.
You can have the warm side of the fire. I'll take it tomorrow.
I'm sorry about earlier. I was tired. Still am.
Can we just start over tomorrow? Like today didn't happen?
I don't want to fight. I just want to sleep.
I'll sleep over there. Don't wait up.
You could have said sorry. You still could.
I don't know why we're even a squad. Not tonight, anyway.
Listening to you three laugh is the best part of the trip.
You're a happy squad. It makes the dark less frightening.
Thank you for letting me sit with you. It feels like family.
A quiet night, I hope. You seem to have it all in hand.
Your fire's very neat. Is that a ninja thing?
I'll sleep well knowing you're watching. Goodnight.
Is someone upset? I don't mean to pry. I just noticed.
Perhaps some tea would help? I brought plenty.
Long days make everyone short-tempered. I'm the same.
I'll sleep closer to the fire, I think. It's a bit frosty tonight. And not only the air.
I don't like to say, but I'm worried about tomorrow if you're not speaking.
Should I say something? I'd better not say something.
That's it! Cover each other, rotate, strike. Beautiful.
You don't need me in this fight. I'll just watch and take notes.
Perfect timing. Again!
Good. Keep your spacing. Call your targets.
Watch your partner's side, not just your own.
Steady. You're doing well. Don't get greedy.
You're stepping on each other! Spread out!
Call it before you throw. You nearly hit your own squad.
Stop going alone. Every one of you. Work together or lose.
Stop fighting each other and fight them!
Nobody's covering anyone! Fall back to me, all of you!
This is what happens when a squad stops trusting itself. Close up!
I go high, you go low! Now!
Got your back! Always got your back!
Just like we practised! Again, again!
I've got this side. You take that one.
Watch out on your right! Got it? Good.
We're holding! Keep holding!
That was mine! Why'd you take that one?
Tell me before you move! I nearly threw at you!
I can't keep track of where you are!
I don't need your help! I've got it myself!
Just stay out of my way!
Fine! Do it your way and see what happens!
You move together like you share one mind!
Look at them! They're wonderful!
I've never felt so safe in the middle of a fight. Odd, isn't it?
Keep going! You're winning, aren't you? It looks like winning.
They're backing off! Good! Good!
I'll stay put. You seem to know what you're doing.
Why are you shouting at each other? Shout at them!
Someone's left that side open! I'm on that side!
Is it going badly? It looks like it's going badly.
Stop arguing! There are people trying to hit us!
Is anyone protecting me? Anyone at all?
I should have hired someone who gets along!
That's teamwork. I can teach technique. That, you found yourselves.
Look at each other. That's the squad that won today. Not luck.
I'm putting "exemplary" in the report. Earn it again next time.
Good work. A solid win, together. Let's keep building on it.
You held. Next time, talk more mid-fight. But you held.
Well done. Check each other for cuts. Then we move on.
We won. Barely. And not because we fought as a squad.
That was luck as much as skill. We'll talk about why later.
Win's a win. But I want better from you. All of you.
We won despite ourselves. That won't hold forever.
If they'd been any better, we'd be carrying someone home. Think about that.
Nobody celebrates. Not until this squad is a squad again.
Best squad in the Leaf! Say it with me! Best squad in the Leaf!
I knew we could do it. All three of us. Together.
That was amazing. You were amazing. We were amazing.
Not bad, us. Not bad at all.
We won! Good job, everyone. Really.
I think we're getting better at this. Don't you?
We won, I suppose. It didn't feel like it.
Okay. That was messy. But we're alive.
Next time, maybe let me finish my move, yeah?
I did that. Me. Not you.
Whatever. It's done. Can we go?
Don't pretend that was teamwork.
You were magnificent together. I'll never forget it.
I could watch you three work all day. Well, not that part. But you know.
Such a fine squad. Your sensei must be so proud.
Well fought, all of you. Thank you.
I'm safe! You did it. I'm very grateful.
That was well done. Shall we carry on?
You won, but goodness, it looked hard.
Thank you. I think. Is everyone all right with each other?
I'm safe. Are you lot? You don't look it.
Well, it's over. I'm not sure how.
You won, but I think you should talk to each other. That's all.
Thank you. Though I'd rather not see that again.
We lost this one together. We'll come back from it together.
You did everything right and it still went wrong. That happens. Remember you stayed a squad.
No blame. Not on anyone. Let's get home.
It didn't go our way. We report it and move on.
Not our day. We'll look at what to change tomorrow.
Nobody's hurt badly. That counts for more than the pay.
We failed because we didn't work together. Hard to hear. True.
Before anyone blames anyone: look at yourselves first. Me included.
Home. Sleep. Then we fix this squad.
This is what a divided squad costs. A mission, today. Something worse, some day.
I won't have this squad fall apart over one failure. Or over pride.
We walk home together. Even if you don't speak, you walk together.
We'll get them next time. Squad promise.
It's not your fault. It's not anybody's fault. We tried.
At least I've got you two. That's worth more than any mission.
It happens. We'll do better next one.
We tried. That's something.
Let's go home and eat something. Everything's better after food.
That went wrong because we weren't listening to each other.
I'm too tired to argue about it. We just lost.
Maybe we're not as good as we thought.
If you'd done what I said, we'd have won.
I'm asking for a different squad. I mean it this time.
Don't talk to me. Not now.
You did your best, and you did it together. I can't ask for more.
It's all right. You looked after each other. And me.
Don't be sad. You're a good squad. Just an unlucky day.
Never mind. These things happen. Thank you anyway.
I'm sorry it didn't work out. I know you tried.
Perhaps another time. Thank you for coming.
It might have gone better if you'd worked together. I'm just saying.
I'm sorry. I don't think it's what any of us wanted.
Go home and rest. And maybe talk.
I'm sorry, but I think it went wrong between you before it went wrong out there.
I'll be asking for a different squad next time.
I hope you sort yourselves out. Truly.
Listen to the whole brief before you ask anything. Half your questions answer themselves.
Read the job, then read it again for what it doesn't say. That's where the trouble lives.
Every mission has a client. The client is the mission. Remember that when you get bored.
Small jobs teach the habits that keep you alive on big ones. Take this seriously.
Questions now, not halfway there. Out on the road, I'd rather you were listening.
That's it? That's the whole mission? I was hoping for something with a scroll in it.
I'm writing it down. Don't look at me like that, I forget things.
Did they say "outside the wall"? Did they actually say that? Yes!
Who gets to carry the map? Not you. You held it upside down last time.
Fine. It's not glamorous. But we're doing it properly. Deal?
You're younger than I expected. No, no, I'm sure you're very good.
I've written it all down for you. Twice, in case you lose one.
Is it always this formal? I thought I'd just ask and you'd come.
Please don't think it's silly. It isn't silly to me.
I can pay. It's all here, counted. I just want it done right.
Last check. Water, wire, rations, bandages. If it isn't on you now, it isn't coming.
Gate in five minutes. Anyone who needs the latrine, this is your moment.
We leave together and we come back together. That's not a rule. It's a promise.
Packs tight, straps short. A rattle is a noise, and noise is a mistake.
Wave goodbye to the gate guards. They count us out and they like to count us in.
I forgot something. I don't know what. I just have the feeling.
My stomach's doing a flip. The good kind. Mostly.
Look, the gate guard's waving at us. We're a real squad now.
Let's make a promise: nobody does anything stupid. I'll start breaking it in an hour.
Bet I can spot the first milestone before you.
Is everyone ready? I've been ready since dawn.
I said goodbye to my family like I was going to war. Silly, isn't it?
Walk on my left, if you would. I'm deaf in the right ear.
I've packed snacks. For all of you. Don't argue.
Right. Off we go. I'll try not to slow you down.
Walk where the ground is hard. Soft ground keeps your footprints and your secrets.
Breathe through your nose. You'll go twice as far before your legs complain.
If you're thirsty, you waited too long. Drink a little, often.
Notice the birds. When they go quiet, something is moving.
We'll stop when I say. Not when your feet say. Your feet are liars.
Want to play a game? First one to see a fox gets the last rice ball.
My sandal strap's rubbing. No, keep going. It's fine. It's not fine.
That cloud looks like the Hokage Rock. Sort of. If you squint.
Tell me something about you I don't know. We've got a long way to go.
I'm not tired. I'm walking slower to save energy. There's a difference.
I never knew the country was this green so close to home.
You don't talk much on the road, do you? I'll talk enough for everyone.
My knees are telling me about every hill. In detail.
Do ninja ever just walk? Without watching every tree?
There used to be a tea stall around this bend. Gone now. Shame.
Stop. Look before you walk in. Exits, people, anything out of place.
We're here. Now the real work starts. The walk was just the walk.
Find the client, confirm the job, then set out your plan. In that order.
First impressions count. Stand up straight, you represent the Leaf.
Note the time. It goes in the report, and it tells us how we paced.
We're actually here! I thought that road would never end.
It looks smaller than I pictured. Everything does, close up.
Okay. Okay. What do we do first? Someone tell me what we do first.
I'm so hungry I could eat this fence. Not now. After. Right.
We made it, all of us. That has to count for something.
Here at last! You can't know how much I've worried about this.
Let me show you around. It won't take long. It's not a big place.
Thank you for coming all this way. Sit, rest, there's tea.
It looks worse than it did yesterday. I'm sure of it.
You came. I half thought nobody would.
Down! Guard the client. Count them before you count on anything.
Backs together. Don't chase anyone into the trees.
Calm. They chose the ground, so we choose the moment.
Watch the flanks. The loud one in front is meant to be watched.
Hold. Hold. Let them come to us.
Behind you! No, other behind!
I knew that bush looked wrong. I knew it!
Stay close. I've got the left. Don't argue, I've got the left.
They picked the wrong squad. Probably. Hopefully.
My hands are shaking. That's fine. They still throw.
What's happening? Who are they? What do I do?
I'll stay down! I'm very good at staying down!
Don't let them take the cart. Or me. Mostly me.
I knew this road was cursed. I said so. Didn't I say so?
Behind the wheel. I'm behind the wheel. Is that right?
That's not in the brief. Good. Now we find out what you're made of.
Plans change. People who can't change with them get hurt. Think.
Take a breath. Then tell me what you see. Not what you expected. What you see.
A job is only simple until it isn't. Stay calm and adjust.
Nobody panics. We've just been given more information. Use it.
Wait, what? That wasn't supposed to happen. Was it?
I take back what I said about this being boring.
Okay. New plan. Does anyone have a new plan?
This is either very bad or very interesting. I can't tell yet.
Nobody told us about this! We're telling the desk about this.
I didn't know! I swear I didn't know about this!
Is that bad? Your faces say it's bad.
That's never happened before. Never. Not once in all my years.
Oh dear. Oh dear, oh dear. What now?
Can you still do it? Please say you can still do it.
Feet first, hands second. A good stance wins more fights than a fast kunai.
Don't stare at the weapon. Watch their shoulders.
Keep moving. Standing still makes you a target.
Breathe out when you strike. Hold your breath and you'll tire twice as fast.
Finish what you start, then look for the next one.
I've got this one! I think I've got this one!
Cover me! Just for a second!
Was that your shuriken? Nice throw!
Left! On your left! Okay, now it's my left!
Is anyone else's heart this loud? Mine's like a drum.
I can't look. Tell me when it's over.
Is it supposed to be that loud?
Good hit! Was that a good hit? It looked like a good hit.
I'm counting them. Three down! No, two. Two and a bit.
Please be careful. I've no idea how to carry you home.
You're bleeding. Fall back. That's an order, not a suggestion.
Pressure on it, now. Pride heals slower than a cut.
Step behind me and get your breath. I'll hold the line.
Wounded fighters make wounded choices. Get out of the front.
Bandage first, bravery after.
You're hurt! Get back, I'll cover you. Go!
Don't you dare pass out on me. Hey. Look at me.
Here, take my bandage roll. I've got another. I think.
Lean on me. Come on. We go together.
That looks bad. Does it hurt? Of course it hurts. Sorry.
You're hurt! Sit down, sit down, I've got a clean cloth.
Stop, please. No job is worth this.
I've seen worse on the farm. Not much worse, though.
Let me help. I'm no medic, but I can hold a bandage.
Here, drink. Water helps. My mother always said water helps.
This one's yours to decide. I'll tell you what I think after, not before.
There's no rule for this. That's why it's hard.
Think about who it helps, who it hurts, and whether you can live with it.
Whatever you pick, own it in the report. Honestly.
Shinobi make calls like this every day. You'll make better ones for having made this one.
I don't know. What would you do? Really?
Whatever you decide, I'm with you. I just want to say that first.
This feels bigger than the brief said. Is it allowed to feel this big?
I'd go the other way. But I'm often wrong. Like, a lot.
Take your time. No, actually, don't take too much time.
It's your call. I'll trust you. I think.
I can't tell you what to do. I can tell you what I hope.
Whatever you choose, I won't hold it against you. Not much.
I've thought about this a hundred times. I still don't know.
Please, think it over. It matters to more people than me.
Fire small, backs to the rock, kit where you can find it in the dark.
First watch is mine. Get your sleep while it's offered.
Dry your socks. Wet feet will end a mission faster than any bandit.
Tell me one thing you'd do differently today. Just one.
Bank the fire before you sleep. Embers by dawn, not ashes.
Do you ever think about what you'll be, after? When we're Jonin and everything?
That owl's been shouting for an hour. Doesn't it sleep?
Swap you my pickled radish for your fish. Please. I'll owe you.
My mattress at home is lumpy. I never thought I'd miss it.
If you wake up and I'm snoring, kick me. Gently.
I haven't slept outdoors since I was a child. I'd forgotten the noise.
Do you take turns watching? All night? You must be so tired.
I brought dried persimmons. Have some. They're better by firelight.
Back home, my family will be having supper about now.
Is it safe to sleep? You'll wake me if it isn't?
Good. Now check yourselves, check the client, then check the ground.
That was clean work. Don't celebrate until we're back inside the wall.
Tie them up properly. Two knots. People slip one.
You held your ground. That's the whole lesson for today.
Nobody down, nobody missing. That's what winning looks like.
We did it! Did you see? We actually did it!
My legs have gone wobbly. Is that normal? Tell me it's normal.
High five. No, the other hand. The one that isn't bleeding.
I'm telling everyone at the Academy about this. Everyone.
We make a good squad. I'm just saying it. Don't make it weird.
Is it over? It's over! Oh, thank goodness.
You were incredible. All of you. I've never seen anything like it.
I'm going to tell this story for the rest of my life.
I take back what I said about you being young.
I didn't run! Did you see? I didn't run.
That's as good as it gets. Remember how it felt. Then do it again.
Clean, quick, careful. If I'd written the plan myself, I'd be pleased with it.
Every box ticked. I don't say this often: I'm proud of you.
That's how a mission should go. Don't let it make you careless next time.
Outstanding. I'll be putting that word in the report. In ink.
That was perfect! Not one thing went wrong. Not one!
Did you see sensei's face? That was almost a smile!
We're legends. Small ones. But legends.
I want to frame this day and hang it on my wall.
Let's do every mission like that. Every single one.
Better than I hoped. Far better. I'll be asking for you by name.
I've never seen a job done so well. I'll tell everyone.
You thought of things I hadn't even thought of. Thank you.
There's extra in the purse. No, take it. You've earned it.
That's the Leaf I was told about. That's exactly it.
Half a job is still a job. Learn from the half you missed.
We got the important part. The rest we'll put down honestly.
Not perfect. Few missions are. What matters is why.
Don't hang your head. Write it down, understand it, do better.
Good enough to pay for, not good enough to brag about. Fair?
We did most of it. Most counts. Doesn't most count?
I keep thinking about the bit we missed. Do you?
Next time we'll get all of it. I'm sure of it.
At least nobody got hurt. That's the main thing, right?
It's not a fail. It's a "nearly". I'm calling it a "nearly".
Not quite what I wanted, but better than nothing. Thank you.
Most of it's done. I can manage the rest myself.
I'm not unhappy. Just a little sorry about the rest.
It's all right. You tried, and it shows.
Half is half more than I could have done alone.
It didn't work. We go home, we report it straight, and we learn from it.
Failing a mission is not failing as a shinobi. Not unless you stop.
I've failed missions. Every Jonin has. Some taught me more than the wins.
Pick yourselves up. We carry this home together.
We'll talk about it tomorrow. Tonight, eat and sleep.
I'm sorry. I should have been faster. I should have been something.
Don't look at me like that. I know. I know.
We'll get another one. There's always another one. Right?
I don't want to go back to the desk. They'll know just from our faces.
At least we were together for it. That's something. Isn't it?
It's all right. Really. You did what you could.
I'm disappointed, I won't lie. But not in you.
Maybe it was never going to work. Maybe I asked too much.
Thank you for coming anyway. Not everyone would have.
Go home safe. That's the main thing.
Report it as it happened, not as you wish it had.
Times, names, what went right, what didn't. Short sentences.
The desk reads every word. Make the words worth reading.
Good report. Clear and honest. That's half of being a shinobi.
Hand it over and stand up straight. You did the work.
Can I hand it in? Please? I want to see the clerk's face.
Do we mention the thing? The thing with the bucket?
I'm so tired I wrote my own name wrong. Twice.
Is the pay today? I've got plans for that pay.
Same time tomorrow? Another one? I'm in if you are.
I came to give my thanks in person. You deserve that.
I've written a note for the desk. All good things.
If I ever need help again, I'm asking for you.
I told the clerk you were wonderful. They didn't look surprised.
Thank you, all of you. I mean it.
Clear the Bandit Camp
C-rank. A bandit camp at {camp} has been robbing the outer farms. {client} brought the complaint. Clear it out. {pay}.
They come down from {camp} every few nights. Took my seed rice, my neighbour's ox, half the village's tools.
There's a lookout at {lookout}. Get past that and the rest are in the hollow.
Thank you. I'll tell the other farms help is coming. They'll sleep tonight.
Good. Be careful. They're rough, and there are more of them than you'd think.
Then we keep sitting up with pitchforks every night. Until something happens.
No? We'll bar the doors and hope. It hasn't worked yet.
Did you see the lookout? Are they still up there?
Smoke from the hollow. They're cooking. That means they're all in.
The camp's empty and our tools are back. You've given the farms their nights back.
Is that my ox? It is! You found my ox! Thank you, all of you.
They're still up there. We'll keep the lamps lit and the dogs loose.
It didn't work. They'll be angrier now. I'm not blaming you. I'm just afraid.
Bandit camp cleared. The farms outside the wall have sent a thank-you in the form of a very large radish. Logged.
C-rank done, everyone back on their own feet. That's the result I like best. Paid.
There are people tied up by the fire. Farmhands. Get them clear before the fighting reaches them.
The leader's running! Straight for the hills, leaving the rest behind. After them!
These aren't bandits. Look at their hands, their boots. Farmers, from a village that burned. Starving.
They're thin as rakes and fighting with hoes. Whatever they've done, these are farmers, not raiders.
Starving farmers, not hardened thieves. Talk them down and show mercy, or arrest them all?
Bear on the Outer Training Grounds
C-rank. A bear has moved into {ground} and won't leave. {client} wants it gone before the squads come back. {pay}.
Big, brown, and sitting in the middle of {ground} like it pays rent. Nobody can train with that out there.
Move it on, back to the hills. Hurt it only if you must. It's just a bear doing bear things.
Good. Don't run if it charges. Or do. I'm not a bear expert.
Thank you. I'll keep everyone off the grounds till you're back.
Then the squads train in the village yards for another week. Crowded and grumpy.
No? Fine. The bear doesn't mind waiting. It's very patient.
Is it still by the target posts? It likes the target posts.
Claw marks on the fence. Fresh ones. It's close.
Gone, back to the hills, and nobody hurt. Including the bear. Good.
The grounds are clear. The squads can come back tomorrow. Thank you.
Still there. Still eating the straw dummies. We'll try again.
It won't budge. Come back when you've rested.
Bear moved on from the outer grounds. The training squads are delighted. The bear, less so. Logged.
C-rank, done. No one mauled. I like a report with no hospital forms attached.
{client}'s beehives at {honey}. A bear will follow honey anywhere. Even away from here.
Cubs in the bushes. Two of them. And their mother knows exactly how close you are.
Giant Boar in the Fields
C-rank. A giant boar is wrecking the farms at {fields}. Track it to its wallow and stop it. {client} is desperate. {pay}.
It's the size of an ox. Tore up three fields and a fence. My children won't go outside.
The tracks lead towards {lair}. Mud, mostly. And broken saplings.
Thank you. Its tusks are as long as my arm. Please, be careful.
Good. Bring it down or drive it off. Either way, I can plant again.
Then we lose the spring crop. We've lost worse. Not much worse.
No? I'll build the fence higher. It'll break it again.
That's its track. See how deep? Heavier than a horse.
The smell from the wallow. You can't miss it.
The fields are safe. The children can play outside again. Thank you.
It's done. I can plant tomorrow. I didn't think I'd be able to say that.
It's still out there, and angry now. We'll keep the children in.
Not today. We'll mend what we can and wait.
Boar dealt with. The farmer sent a basket of turnips. I'm told that's the highest honour. Logged.
C-rank, done. That's a field that will feed people this summer. Good work.
Piglets. A whole litter, tucked behind her. She's a mother, and she's been driven out of her own forest.
A second set of tracks crosses the first. Bigger. There are two of them.
A mother with piglets, driven from her forest. Drive her off somewhere safe, or fight to end the threat?
Wolves at the Outer Farms
C-rank. Wolves are taking livestock from the outer farms at night. Guard {pen}, then find the den. {pay}.
Three goats and a calf this week. They come after midnight, quiet as smoke. My dogs are terrified.
Watch {pen} tonight. When they come, follow them home. The den's somewhere above {den}.
Thank you. I'll leave a lamp in the window. Don't let it fool you, I'll be hiding under the bed.
Good. Take my lantern. And this stick. It's a good stick.
Then we lose another goat tonight. And tomorrow.
No? We'll bring the animals into the house. It's crowded, but it's safe.
Did you hear them? Out past the stream. Howling.
Tracks in the frost. Five, maybe six of them.
Not a single animal taken last night. First time in weeks. Thank you.
The wolves are gone from the hills above us. I don't know how you did it. Thank you.
Another pen broken. We'll keep watch ourselves. It's all we can do.
They're still out there. Come back when you're ready. Please.
Wolf trouble at the outer farms, settled. You look like you've been up all night. Because you have. Logged.
C-rank, done. The farmers say the hills are quiet again. Paid.
Smoke on the hills above the den. Campfires. A bandit gang's fires drove the wolves down to the farms.
That wolf at the front. It's the size of a pony. The rest of the pack follow it like a shadow.
Bodyguard for a Noble Child
C-rank. A visiting noble, {client}, wants a squad to guard their child for a day in the village, from {inn} to {market}. {pay}.
My child wants to see the village. The market, the shops, the Hokage Rock. Keep them safe and keep them happy.
We stay at {inn}. Collect the child there at nine. Return by sunset, and not a moment later.
Very good. My child is curious, and has no sense of danger. That is your job.
Excellent. Do try to make it fun. The last guards were dreadfully dull.
How disappointing. We will tour the village with our own guards, I suppose.
I see. The Leaf is busier than I was told.
Is my child enjoying the day? Good. And safe? Better.
They wrote to me already. "Bought a wooden kunai." I did not approve that.
Home safe and full of stories. My child says the Leaf is the best place in the world. Thank you.
A happy day and not a hair out of place. You have my gratitude, and my good word with your Hokage.
My child is safe, but it was too close. I expected better from the Leaf.
We will be leaving early. I'm sure you understand.
Noble child, returned in one piece. {client} sent a very formal letter. Mostly polite. Logged.
Bodyguard C-rank, done. A happy child and a calm parent. Diplomacy on legs. Good work.
The child was right here a second ago. Gone. Slipped off to see the village alone.
Those men by the stall have been following since the inn. Someone's paid them to take the child.
Race for the Cat Burglar
C-rank, contested. A cat burglar's working {rooftops}. I've sent two squads. First to bring them in gets the pay: {pay}.
Six houses this month, always the rooftops, always gone before the dogs bark. The other squad left ten minutes ago.
The burglar's hideout is somewhere around {hideout}. Nobody's found it. Yet.
Good. Run. The other squad is already out the door.
Right. Bring them in alive, unbruised if possible, and before the others do.
Then the other squad takes it uncontested. Easy money for them.
No? I'll tell them they've got the whole field. They'll be smug.
Sighted on the bakery roof ten minutes ago. Heading east.
The other squad came past here at a sprint. They're ahead of you.
Caught, and before the other squad! The rooftops are safe again.
You beat them to it. They'll be sulking for a week.
The burglar's slipped away, and the other squad's still looking. Not today.
The other squad got there first. Shake hands. It's still the Leaf.
Cat burglar, in custody. And you beat the other squad. I'm not supposed to have favourites. I do. Logged.
Contest closed. The rooftops are quiet. Pay's yours.
That tip about the east alley was {rival_squad}'s doing. Wrong street. Deliberately.
The burglar's too quick for either squad alone. {rival_squad} are nodding. Work together, split the credit.
Sealed Message to the Border Post
C-rank. Rush a sealed message to {post} within the day. Through {pass}, no stops. {pay}.
Sealed, and stays sealed. Hand it to the post commander at {post}. Nobody else.
Take the pass at {pass}. It's the fastest way, which is also why it's the one people watch.
Good. Here's the case. It doesn't leave your body until you're at the post.
Right. Run light, eat on the move. Sleep when you're back.
Then I send it with the next squad and hope it's not too late.
No? It'll have to wait. The border hates waiting.
At the pass already? Good time. Keep moving.
The seal's still whole? Good. Don't stop to look at it every mile.
Delivered, sealed, inside the day. The post commander sends thanks.
Clean run. Exactly how a courier mission should go.
Too late for it to matter. We'll find another way.
The message didn't get through. Come back and we'll talk about what happened.
Courier run, done. The border post says the seal was intact and the runners looked exhausted. Both good signs. Logged.
Message delivered on time. Go and sleep. You've earned that before the pay.
Two figures at the pass, waiting, watching the road. Scouts, and they know exactly what you're carrying.
The commander wants you to wait. There's an answer to carry back, and it's being written now.
Medicine for the Border Village
C-rank, two days. Medicine and supplies for the healer at {healer}, by the hill road at {road}. {pay}.
Fever remedies, bandages, a crate of salves. The border village's healer is nearly out of everything.
The crates are fragile and the road at {road} is rough. Slow on the hills, quick on the flat.
Thank you. There are people waiting on this. Real people. Children.
Good. The cart's loaded. The horse is called Biscuit. Don't ask me why.
Then I'll send it with a trader and pray it arrives.
No? I'll wait for another squad. The healer can't wait long.
Crates all still roped? Check the knots at every stop.
Halfway. The healer will have sent someone to watch the road for you.
Every crate delivered. The healer wrote to say three fevers broke the first night.
It got there. All of it. You've no idea how many people that helps.
Not everything arrived. The healer will make do. They always do, out there.
It didn't get through. We'll send another cart. Thank you for trying.
Medical delivery to the border, done. The healer sent a letter. It's mostly gratitude and a list of what to send next. Logged.
C-rank, done. That's medicine where it was needed. The best kind of mission.
The cart's lighter. You turned your back to water the horse and two crates are gone.
Thugs on the only bridge, with a sign and a box. A "toll", they say. For crossing their bridge.
The sky's gone black over the pass. Storm. Get the cart under the overhang and wait it out.
Pay the thugs' toll and keep the medicine moving, or fight your way across the bridge?
Kiln Pottery to the Border Market
C-rank, two days. The kiln family's best pottery from {kiln} to the market at {market}, unbroken. {pay}.
This is a year's best work. Packed in straw, roped in crates. Not one chip, please, or it's worthless.
The road at {road} has a reputation. Thieves know what good pottery fetches at the border.
Thank you. Drive the cart like it's carrying eggs. Because it might as well be.
Good. If anyone asks what's in the crates, say turnips.
Then we miss the market. A year's work sits in the shed.
No? I'll wait for the next squad. The market won't wait long.
Still ringing true when you tap the crates? Good.
Halfway to {market}. Slow on the downhill.
Every piece arrived whole. They sold out by noon on the first day. Thank you.
Not a crack. My grandmother would have hugged you. I might.
Broken. Half of it. A year's work in shards on the road.
It didn't reach the market. We'll start again. Potters always start again.
Pottery delivered whole. That's harder than any fight, if you ask me. Logged.
C-rank, done. {client} says the market bought every piece. Good work.
Rope across the road and figures in the trees. Thieves, and they know what's under that straw.
A rival workshop's master is shouting across the market: the glaze on these pots was stolen from them.
Supplies to the Hill Outpost
C-rank, two days. A cart of supplies to the watch outpost at {outpost}, up the trail at {trail}. {pay}.
Rice, oil, bandages and arrows. The outpost has been on short rations for a week.
The trail at {trail} is steep and narrow. Mind the cart wheels on the switchbacks.
Good. The watch up there will be glad to see you. They don't get many visitors.
Right. Load is checked. Go.
Then the outpost tightens its belt another notch. They're used to it.
No? I'll find a squad that will. Soon, I hope.
Switchbacks ahead. Push from the back, pull from the front.
The outpost will have seen your dust by now.
Supplies delivered. The watch sends thanks and a request for more pickles next time.
The outpost is stocked for a month. Good work.
The supplies didn't reach the top. The outpost will be hungry.
Not today. We'll send another cart. Rest first.
Outpost supplied. The Chunin up there wrote "thank you" in very large letters. Logged.
C-rank, done. A fed outpost is a watchful outpost. Paid.
Half the outpost is flat on their mats with fever. The ones still standing are swaying.
The cart road's gone. A landslide took it overnight. The crates go up the rest of the way by hand.
The Signboard Taker
C-rank. A wandering swordsman is beating the village's dojos one by one and taking their signboards. {client} wants it stopped. {pay}.
Four dojos beaten. Four signboards taken. A challenge notice was nailed to {dojo} this morning.
The Gekko don't hire help for swords. But this one is good, and we're tired of losing boards.
Good. Watch the footwork, not the blade. The blade lies. The feet don't.
Thank you. Bring the signboards home. They mean more than they look.
Then the swordsman takes another board tonight.
Understood. We'll face it ourselves. We'll lose, but we'll face it.
The challenge notice says sunset. Be there early.
Not every swordsman is what they seem. Watch the sleeves.
The signboards are back on their walls. Every dojo in the Leaf owes you.
Well fought. The Gekko will remember this.
Another board gone. We'll train harder. That's all we can do.
Not today. The swordsman is still out there. So are we.
Dojo challenge, settled. The signboards are home. {client} bowed to me. I didn't know what to do. Logged.
C-rank, done. The dojos are calling it a fine duel. Pay's here.
The swordsman kneels and lays the blade down. All this was only for a worthy opponent. And now, a request: to be taught.
A glint at the swordsman's sleeve. Needles, and the tips are wet. Poison.
Beaten, the swordsman waits. Take the signboards and send them off, or agree to teach them?
Escort a Trader, East Road
C-rank, two days. Escort {client} and a cart of goods along the east road to {waystation}. Bandits reported near {bend}. {pay}.
Silk, salt and lacquer boxes, all the way to {waystation}. Two days on the east road. I've heard stories about that road.
We'll camp at {camp} the first night. Then the bridge, then the waystation. Easy, if nothing happens.
Good. I walk slowly and talk a lot. You'll get used to both.
Excellent. I'll pay for the first night's meal at the waystation. A good one.
Then I'll go alone. Or not go. Probably not go.
No? I'll ask another squad. Or hire some muscle in the market. Cheaper, louder.
Is that the bend? I always hold my breath at the bend.
The cart's holding up. The axle grumbles, but it always grumbles.
The waystation! And every box intact. You're the best escort I've ever paid for.
We made it. I'll tell every trader on this road to ask for your squad.
We lost half the cart. I'm alive, though. That counts for something.
It didn't go well. I'll turn back. Thank you for keeping me breathing.
Escort to the east waystation, done. {client} sent a bolt of silk for the desk. It's very nice. Logged.
C-rank complete. Trader safe, goods safe, squad home. That's the whole job.
The bridge is gone. Washed out. The ford's the only way now, and it's slow and open on both sides.
Movement past the firelight. They've come back, at night, for the cart.
A traveller on the road, alone, begging to walk with the cart. For safety, they say.
One bandit didn't run. Tied up by the cart, they swear they'll never come back. Hand them over at the waystation, or let them go?
Escort a Scholar to the Border
C-rank, two days. Escort {client}, a scholar, through the hills to {village}. The road goes over {pass}. {pay}.
I have business in the border village. Books to see, people to ask. I've never walked the hills before.
Two days, they tell me. Over {pass}, a night at {camp}, then down to {village}. How hard can it be?
Splendid. I've packed three books and one spare sock. Is that enough?
Thank you. I promise to complain only about the important things.
Then I'll wait for the next squad. My research has waited this long.
No? I'll read about the hills instead. Much less walking.
Is it always this steep? Don't answer that.
I've filled four pages with notes already. The wildflowers here are extraordinary.
We're here. I can't feel my feet, but we're here. Thank you, truly.
Safe in the border village, and with my books dry. You're a credit to the Leaf.
I'll go home. The hills won this time. Thank you for getting me back.
It didn't work out. I'm not cut out for mountains, it seems.
Scholar delivered safely. {client} wrote a whole page about how brave you were. It's quite flowery. Logged.
C-rank, done. A client who arrived healthier than they left. That's good escort work.
{client} is pale and sweating at the pass, sitting down every ten steps. The hills have got to them.
By the fire, {client} goes quiet, then admits the real reason for the trip. Harmless, and private. "Please don't tell anyone."
{client} asked you to keep the secret. Keep it, or put it in the mission report?
Guard a Caravan, East Road
C-rank, two days. Guard {client}'s three-cart caravan on the east road as far as {waystation}. Raiders are active. {pay}.
Three carts, two drivers I trust, and a lot of road. We camp at {camp} and reach {waystation} the second evening.
The raiders on this road hit fast and run. Keep your eyes on the treeline and your hands near your kunai.
Good. You'll ride the middle cart. Best view, worst seat.
Thank you. My drivers are {hand_a} and {hand_b}. They know the road. Listen to them.
Then I'll wait. The goods will wait too, more or less.
No? I'll double the drivers and hope for the best.
First day done. We're on schedule. Don't jinx it.
The oxen are nervous. They smell something we don't.
Three carts in, three carts whole. I'll hire your squad again, for every trip.
Every crate accounted for at the waystation. That's a good guard.
We lost a cart. Maybe more. At least we're alive.
It went badly. I'll be counting losses for a week.
Caravan guarded to the waystation. {client} is ordering their next run through us. Logged.
C-rank, done. Two days, three carts, one tired squad. Paid.
A mirror flash from the second cart. Someone in the caravan is signalling the raiders.
This wheel's been cut halfway through. Clean cut, fresh sawdust. Somebody did it in the night.
The signals came from inside the caravan. Accuse {hand_a}, accuse {hand_b}, or say nothing until you're sure?
Festival Watch: Pickpockets
C-rank. A pickpocket gang is working the festival crowd on {street}. {client} wants it stopped tonight. {pay}.
Four purses gone last night and three the night before. They work in pairs. One bumps, one lifts.
Walk the crowd on {street}. Watch the hands, not the faces. Faces always look innocent.
Good. Wear something festive. A squad in uniform scares the thieves off before you can catch them.
Thank you. If you can, enjoy a little of the festival too. Just a little.
Then I'll warn people to hold their purses tight and hope.
No? The gang will have a very good night, then.
Anything? I saw a pair near the goldfish stall acting oddly.
Another purse gone by the lantern arch. They're bold.
The gang's caught and the purses are back with their owners. The festival can breathe.
A quiet night! Not one purse lost after you caught them. Thank you.
They got away with half the market's takings. We'll do better next year.
Not tonight. They're slippery. Thank you for trying.
Pickpocket gang, caught. Did you at least eat some yakitori while you were out there? Logged.
C-rank, done. The festival committee is very relieved. Paid.
The purses were a distraction. The gang's real target is the fireworks crate behind the stage.
{guest}'s child has slipped the guards to see the stalls alone. Somewhere in this crowd.
Smugglers at the Ford
C-rank, night work. A smuggling crew crosses the river at {ford} after dark. Hide in {hide}, wait, and stop them. {pay}.
Untaxed metal, mostly. Bad blades that undercut honest smiths. They cross {ford} at moonrise.
The reeds at {hide} are good cover. Cold and wet, but good cover.
Good. Dark clothes, no lamps. And don't sneeze.
Thank you. The Hagane forges can't compete with stolen metal. Stop them.
Then they cross again tonight, and the night after.
No? I'll report it to the guard again. They'll do nothing again.
Moonrise soon. Stay low in the reeds.
Hear that? Oars. Quiet ones. They're coming.
The crew's caught and the cargo seized. The honest forges thank you.
That ford will be quiet for a long while now. Good.
They crossed. We'll see their blades in the market by next week.
Not tonight. They were quicker than we thought.
Smuggling crew, stopped. You're wet to the waist. Reeds, was it? Logged.
C-rank, done. {client} says the forge district will sleep easier. Paid.
Not metal. The crates are full of animals. Rare ones, crammed into cages far too small.
The first boat's empty. A decoy. The real one is crossing downstream right now!
Cramped cages full of rare animals. Free them here by the river, or hand them over as evidence?
The Haunted Waystation Inn
C-rank, two days. The inn at {inn} has a ghost story, and travellers who never checked out. {client} wants it looked into. {pay}.
Footsteps at night, cold drafts, a face at the window. Guests leave in the dark without paying. Some don't leave at all.
Stay a night at {inn}. See it for yourselves. And please, please tell me it's not real.
Thank you. Your rooms are free, of course. Room six is the worst one. You're in room six.
Good. Don't go in the cellar alone. Don't go in the cellar at all, actually.
Then I'll lose more guests. And maybe my mind.
No? I'll ask the priest to come again. It didn't work last time.
Did you hear it last night? The knocking? Tell me you heard it.
Cold spot on the stairs again. I don't go up there after dark.
No ghost. Just people, and they're gone now. My inn is mine again.
I can sleep through the night! I've forgotten what that feels like. Thank you.
The knocking's still there. Maybe it is a ghost. Maybe I'll sell.
Nothing solved. I'll keep the lamps lit all night again.
Haunted inn, investigated. No ghosts on file. I'm relieved. I don't know what form I'd use. Logged.
C-rank, done. The waystation inn is open for business, minus the haunting. Paid.
Fresh footprints in the cellar dust, and a passage behind the casks. A gang has been robbing the sleeping guests.
{client} finally admits it: grandfather made the ghost up, years ago, to bring curious guests in. It worked too well.
Stakeout: Warehouse Thefts
C-rank. Goods keep vanishing from {warehouse}. Interview the staff, stake it out, find out who. {pay}.
A crate a week, never more. No broken locks. Whoever it is has a key, or knows where one hangs.
Three people work nights: {night_guard}, {clerk} and {porter}. I trust them all. That's the problem.
Thank you. Be fair to them. Whoever it isn't deserves that.
Good. Watch the back door. That's where I'd go.
Then I'll change the locks and hope. Again.
No? I'll keep counting crates and losing sleep.
Have you spoken to all three yet? What did they say?
Another crate missing last night. Right under our noses.
Now I know. It hurts, but I know. Thank you.
The thefts have stopped. The warehouse feels like mine again.
Still vanishing. I'll be suspecting everyone forever now.
No answer. I'll have to look at all of them differently. I hate that.
Warehouse thefts, solved. {client} is relieved and a little sad. That's how these usually end. Logged.
C-rank, done. Stakeouts are mostly waiting. You waited well. Paid.
The key that opens the back door hangs on {night_guard}'s belt. And the mud on those sandals matches the alley.
The ledger's been changed in {clerk}'s hand. Every missing crate, written out of the books afterwards.
{porter} carries crates out every night, and one more always goes out the back than came in the front.
You've heard all three and seen the clues. Name the thief: {night_guard}, {clerk} or {porter}?
Keep the Peace at the Stream
C-rank. Two hamlets near the border are fighting over {stream}. Keep the peace until the magistrate comes. {client} asked for us. {pay}.
They've dammed {stream} above our fields. My rice is drying out. {other_headman} says it was always theirs.
Hear us both, if you must. Just make sure nobody gets hurt before the magistrate arrives.
Thank you. You'll see we're in the right. Look at our fields.
Good. My people are angry. Your being here will calm them.
Then someone will get hurt. I can feel it coming.
No? The magistrate is a week away. It's a long week.
Did you talk to {other_headman}? What did they say? Lies, I expect.
The weir is still blocked. My people are gathering with spades.
Water flows to both hamlets. Nobody hurt. The magistrate will have little to do.
Peace. Fragile, but peace. Thank you for listening to both of us.
It came to blows. The magistrate will have a lot to say.
Nothing settled. Both sides angrier than before.
Water dispute, calmed. The magistrate arrived to find almost nothing to do. That's a compliment. Logged.
C-rank, done. Diplomacy is harder than fighting. You managed it. Paid.
Strangers with clubs on the weir. One headman has hired muscle to settle the stream by force.
Look at the banks. Cracked mud a hand's width down. It's a dry season, and there's barely enough for one hamlet.
The magistrate isn't here yet, and someone must decide. Share the water, give it upstream, or give it downstream?
Border Patrol with a Chunin
C-rank. Walk a stretch of the border with {client}, checking the markers at {markers} and the watch at {post}. {pay}.
We walk the line from {markers} to {post}. Every stone checked, every post visited. It's long and mostly dull.
Mostly. If you see someone on the wrong side of a marker, you tell me before you do anything.
Good. Bring water and good sandals. We'll walk a long way.
Right. Quiet on the line. Voices carry along the ridge.
Fine. I'll walk it alone. It's quieter that way.
No? Another squad will come. The border isn't going anywhere.
That's the fourth marker. Straight and unmoved. Good.
The watch post is past the next ridge. Keep pace.
Line walked, markers checked, posts visited. A clean patrol.
Good work. You kept your eyes open. That's all a patrol really is.
We'll turn back. The patrol's compromised. Report it as it happened.
Not a clean walk. We'll report it and send another squad.
Border patrol, done. {client} says your squad kept up and kept quiet. Logged.
C-rank complete. The line is where it should be. Paid.
Two figures by the watch post with a drawing board. Foreign scouts, mapping every post on the line.
{lost} is crouched beyond the marker stones, a Genin from another village, lost and very frightened.
Guard a Shop Through the Sale
C-rank. {client} at {shop} is being threatened by a rival's hired thugs. Protect the shop through the week's big sale. {pay}.
They broke a window last week and told my customers to shop elsewhere. My stall, at {shop}. My living.
I know who's paying them. {rival}. Nobody will say so out loud.
Thank you. Stand where people can see you. That alone might be enough.
Good. If they come, they come at closing. That's when they always come.
Then I'll close for the week. And lose the sale, and maybe the shop.
No? I'll board the windows and pray.
They walked past twice this morning. Looking. Just looking.
Sales are good! People feel safe with a squad here.
The sale's over and the shop's whole. Best week I've had all year.
No broken windows, no frightened customers. Thank you.
They got in. Broken stock, frightened customers. I don't know what I'll do.
It didn't work. Maybe nothing would have. Thank you for standing with me.
Shop protected through the sale. The market's talking about it. Logged.
C-rank, done. Sometimes guarding is about standing still and being seen. Paid.
The rival's man leans close. Twice the fee to be somewhere else at closing. Coins already in hand.
The ledger tells a different story. {client} started this feud, years ago, by undercutting {rival}.
Twice the fee to look away. Refuse the coins, or take them?
Both shopkeepers share the blame. Bring them together to talk it out, or stand by your client?
Recover a Stolen Heirloom
C-rank. {client}'s family heirloom was stolen and turned up at a pawnshop in the border village, at {pawn}. Recover it. {pay}.
A lacquered box, black with a gold crane on the lid. My family has kept it for five generations.
Someone saw it in the back of {pawn}. They won't sell it back. They say they never had it.
Thank you. It's not worth much to anyone else. It's worth everything to us.
Good. The pawnbroker isn't alone. There's a whole ring behind that counter. Be careful.
Then it's gone. Five generations, and I'm the one who lost it.
No? I'll keep writing to the magistrate. For all the good it does.
Did you see it? Is it there? Is it whole?
The ledger says they bought it a month ago. From whom, I wonder.
That's it. That's the crane. Thank you. You've no idea.
Home. Back on the shelf where it belongs. My grandmother would weep.
It's still in their hands. Or sold on. I'll never know.
Gone. Thank you for trying. It mattered that someone tried.
Heirloom recovered. {client} came by to say thank you in person. Twice. Logged.
C-rank, done. Some things matter far more than their price. Paid.
This box in the back room is a copy. Wrong weight, wrong lacquer. The real one is out on the counter, in plain sight.
Boots on the stairs. The pawnbroker's men are back early, and the back room has one door.
Find the Missing Woodcutter
C-rank, rescue. A woodcutter didn't come home from {woods} last night. {client}'s household is frantic. Find them. {pay}.
Our woodcutter went up the path at {woods} yesterday morning and never came back. The axe is gone too.
Follow the path. There'll be fresh chips where the cutting stopped. Please hurry.
Thank you. Take this blanket. And this water. And please, please hurry.
Good. I'll keep the fire high so you can see the house from the hill.
Then I'll go up myself. In the dark, if I have to.
No? We'll gather the neighbours with torches.
Any sign? Chips, footprints? Anything?
The light's going. Please keep looking.
Home! Hurt, but home. Thank you. I'll never forget this.
You found them. Alive. I don't know how to thank you.
Nothing. We'll keep searching at first light.
You came back without them. I know you tried. I know.
Missing woodcutter, found and home. The hospital says a broken leg and a lot of luck. Logged.
C-rank rescue, done. The best reports are the ones where everyone comes home. Paid.
A shout from below. The woodcutter fell into the ravine at {ravine}, and the only way down is the cliff face.
Howling, closer than it should be. The wolves smelled the blood before you found the woodcutter.
Track the Thief into the Forest
C-rank. A thief robbed {client}'s stall at {shop} and fled into the forest along {forest}. Track them down. {pay}.
Grabbed the cash box and a sack of rice, then ran for the trees at {forest}. Fast, and small.
The tracks start at my back door. After that, the forest. I don't know the forest.
Thank you. The box has my mark on the lid. A circle with a line.
Good. Bring my money back. And the rice, if it's still whole.
Then it's gone. A month's takings, gone.
No? I'll put a lock on the door. Too late, as always.
Found the trail? Good. It was going towards the stream when I lost it.
The forest's thick out there. Don't get lost yourselves.
My box! And most of the coins. Thank you. I didn't think I'd see it again.
Found, and brought back. You're better at this than the guards.
The trail went cold. So did my hopes. Thank you anyway.
Gone into the forest for good, then. I'll start saving again.
Thief tracked and stall money returned. You've pine needles in your collar. Logged.
C-rank, done. Tracking's patience more than speed. You had both. Paid.
The tracks stop dead at the stream. The thief doubled back through the water to throw off the dogs.
The thief is a child. Thin, frightened, guarding the rice like treasure. It was for a sick parent at home.
A runaway child stealing for a sick parent. Bring them in as the job says, or plead their case to {client}?
Target Practice, Youngest Year
An Academy teacher, {client}, needs extra hands for the youngest year's target practice in {yard}. {pay}.
Thirty first-years and one of me. Set the targets in {yard}, then walk the line and fix their grips.
Mind their elbows, not their aim. Aim comes later. Bad elbows last forever.
Wonderful. The little ones will be thrilled. Try not to look too impressive, they'll copy everything.
Good. Bring patience. Somebody always throws backwards on the first day.

Not many baskets today. Never mind. The tree will try again next autumn.
Orchard job, done. There's a persimmon on my desk now. I'm choosing to think it's for me.
{client} says the top branches are bare for the first time in years. Logged.
A wasp nest hangs in the best tree, right where the ripest fruit is. Of course it does.
A child climbed up after you and now won't move. Clinging to a branch, very high, very quiet.

The hospital needs medicinal herbs from {slope}. {client} of the Suzuran will show you which. Deliver to {hospital}. {pay}.
Feverfew, mugwort, the little blue-flowered one. Here's a drawing. Cut above the root so it grows back.
Bring them to {hospital} before evening. Wilted herbs lose half their good.
Good. Here's a knife and a cloth bag. Not a sack. They bruise in a sack.
Thank you. My family has gathered on that slope for six generations. Treat it kindly.
Understood. I'll go myself at dawn. The herbs are best then anyway.
No? The medics will make do with dried stock for another week.
That's the right leaf. See the fine hairs underneath? Good eye.
Leave a few plants in every patch. Always leave some for next year.
A full bag, every one the right plant. The hospital will be very glad.
Clean cuts, fresh leaves. You'd make a fine herbalist, if you ever tire of kunai.
Too few, and some of these are wilted. We'll go again tomorrow.
Not enough for the hospital's order. It happens. The slope will keep.
Herbs delivered to the hospital. You smell of mint and mud. Logged.
{client} checked every stem and found nothing wrong. That's the Suzuran stamp of approval.
Wait. These two leaves look the same, but one smells bitter. A poisonous lookalike. Check every stem.
The best patch on the slope has a snake coiled right in the middle of it, sunning itself.
Orderly, One Day on the Wards
The hospital wants orderlies for a day on {ward}. Linens, meals, errands for the medics. {client} will meet you. {pay}.
Fresh sheets on every bed in {ward}, meals at noon and six, and run where the medics send you.
Speak softly, walk softly. Some of these patients haven't slept in days.
Thank you. Wash your hands at the basin. Every time you enter a room.
Good. If anyone asks you a medical question, fetch a medic. Don't guess.
We'll stretch the shift, then. We always do.
Understood. The wards will manage, somehow.
The sheets in room four are done? Good. Room five needs water.
The patient by the window says you're very polite. Keep it up.
Every bed clean, every meal served. The medics got their breaks for once.
You were a real help today. The patients noticed. So did I.
A hard shift, and some things fell through. Go home. Rest. Hospitals are like that.
Not the smoothest day. Nobody was hurt by it, though. That's what matters here.
Orderly shift, done. The medics asked if you could come back. Twice.
Hospital job, logged. Don't worry, that smell of disinfectant fades in a day.
Bed twelve is empty. {wanderer} has wandered out in slippers and a gown, and could be anywhere.
The medics are out of a herb only the Suzuran gardens grow. Run to {garden} for more.

The washers at {bank} have the inn's laundry and too few hands. Wash, wring, dry, deliver to {inn}. {pay}.
Sheets from {inn}, a mountain of them. Scrub on the stones, rinse downstream, wring till your arms ache.
Whites first, coloured last, never together. The inn counts every sheet back.
Good! Roll your trousers up, the water's cold this time of year.
Here's a washboard. You'll be singing the washing songs by noon. Everyone does.
More scrubbing for us, then. Our hands are tough. They'd have to be.
No? The inn's guests will sleep on yesterday's sheets. Not our problem.
Wring it harder! Like it owes you money.
That's the third basket. Hang them high, where the wind is.
Every sheet white and dry and folded. The inn will think we've hired magic.
Lovely work. Come back any washing day. We'll teach you the second verse.
Damp sheets going back to the inn. They'll complain. They always complain.
Not our best load. The river's had worse from us.
Laundry, delivered. Your hands are wrinkled like a dried plum. Logged.
{client} says you can wring a sheet properly. That's not nothing.
A gust just took a whole sheet off the line. It's sailing over the rooftops like a kite!
Someone washed a red sash with the whites. Pink, everywhere. Find which loads can still be saved.
Moving Day Across the Village
{client}'s family is moving from {old} to {new}. Boxes, furniture, and a great deal of advice. {pay}.
Everything from {old} to {new} by dark. Boxes are labelled. Mostly labelled.
Kitchen first. If we can cook tonight, we can survive anything.
Thank you! Mind the doorframe. It's lower than it looks.
Good. The boxes marked with a circle are fragile. Or is it the cross? Ask me again.
Then it'll take us three days instead of one. Wonderful.
No? We'll call the cousins. They always break something.
The kitchen's in! Now the futons. Then the rest.
Careful round that corner! No, the other corner.
Everything moved, nothing broken. We're home. A new home. Thank you.
The tea's already brewing in the new kitchen. Sit, please. You've earned it.
Half here, half there. We'll sleep in the old house one more night.
Something's broken, and we're not finished. It's still a new start. We'll get there.
Moving day, logged. You can stop carrying things now. That's a chair, not a box. Put it down.
{client} says the move went smoother than their wedding. That's a compliment, I think.
Grandmother's tea set goes by hand. Only by hand. Not in a box, not on the cart. Walk slow.
The cat does not want to move. It's found the one spot in the house nobody ever looks.
This old chest won't budge for anyone. It'll take chakra in the arms to get it off the floor.

The records room at {room} has a season of mission reports to sort. By rank, then by date. {pay}.
D-ranks on the low shelves, C-ranks above. Date order. Use the tags, not the handwriting.
No reading for fun. Well. A little. Everyone does. Just keep sorting while you do it.
Good. Dust masks are in the drawer. You'll want one by the third shelf.
Excellent. I've been dreading this for a month. Here's the ledger.
Then the pile grows. It always grows.
No? I'll sort them myself in my sleep. I already dream about them.

Some of these reports are written in pencil. Pencil! Put those in the box for recopying.
Every shelf in order. I could find a report from last month blindfolded. Thank you.
Perfect. I'll write your names in the log of the room. Very small. Next to the date.
Half sorted, half muddled. We'll finish another week. The shelves won't run away.

{client} says the shelves are in order. We'll see when I next find a file in under a minute.

Little grey moths, all along the bottom shelf. Paper moths. They've been eating the old reports.

{client} needs every item in {store} counted before the quarterly tax visit. Bring an abacus. {pay}.

Count twice, write once. And don't move anything, I know where it all is.
Good. Here's the ledger. Neat numbers, please. Sevens with a line through them.

No? Then I'll pray the collector is in a good mood.
Back shelf done? Good. The barrels are next.

A perfect ledger. I'll sleep tonight for the first time this week.
The numbers won't come right. I'll have to explain to the collector myself.
Not finished. I'll stay up with it. Thank you anyway.
Inventory, done. You count better than half the clerks here. Don't tell them.
{client} says the ledger's spotless. Logged before tax day, even.

The Inuzuka clinic wants its boarding ninken walked along {route} and every one brought back. Every one. {pay}.

Anything? Paw prints? Fur on a fence?

Pet sitting, signed off. Fur on your sleeves and a scratch on your hand. Standard.
{client} says the animals were in better shape than when they left. Logged.

{neighbour} is at the fence, furious. Says this pet has been raiding their garden for weeks.

{client} needs the fence at {fence} mended. Posts from {yard}, the rest is hammer and patience. {pay}.

Same line as before. Exactly the same. I don't want any trouble with the neighbours.
Good. Hammer's in the shed. Mind the roses.
Thank you. I'll bring tea when you get to the corner post. That's the hard one.

No? Fine. I'll prop it up with a broom like before.
That post's straight? Let me look. Yes. Good.
The neighbour keeps peeking over. Just smile and keep hammering.
Straight and strong. That fence will outlast me. Thank you.
A fine fence. Even the neighbour said so. Grudgingly.
Still leaning, but less. I'll take less.
Not finished. We'll prop it for now. Thank you for trying.
Fence mended. No neighbour complaints filed. A miracle. Logged.
{client} says the fence is straight and the neighbours are still talking to each other. Nice work.
{neighbour} says the fence has always stood a hand's width too far onto their side. Always.
This post crumbles like a biscuit when you touch it. Termites. The old posts are hollow.
{client} and {neighbour} both want the line their way. Split it fair, or side with one of them?

{client}'s roof at {roof} is leaking and the rain's due tonight. Tiles from {yard}. {pay}.

Good. Ladder's round the side. Or do you just walk up walls?
Thank you. Watch the ridge, it's slippery with moss.
Then it's buckets on the floor again tonight.
No? I'll move the futon. Again. It's practically on wheels.
How many tiles left? The clouds are coming in.
I can hear you up there. Is that hammering, or falling?

Still leaking, but slower. I'll take slower.
Roof repaired. You're damp at the edges. Close call, was it? Logged.
{client} says the house stayed dry all night. Paid in full.
A swallow has built its nest right over the leak. With eggs in it. Move it, very carefully.
The neighbour's cat followed you up the ladder and won't come down. It's yowling at the gutter.
First drops, right on time, and four tiles still to go. Faster!

The river's cold at dawn. Wear something you don't mind smelling of fish forever.
Good. Dawn means dawn, not after breakfast.
Here's a pair of gloves. Your hands will thank me by the third net.

Heave! Heave! Keep the line even.
That's a good basket. Silver all the way down.

Not much in the nets today. The river gives what it gives.

The river below the market bridge is a mess. {client} wants it cleared from {bank}. Nets and sacks provided. {pay}.

Good. Here's a net on a pole. Long reach. You'll need it.
Thank you. Sacks by the steps. Rubbish in, fish out.
Fine. The river will carry it off eventually. To the next village.
No? I'll keep picking at it on my days off.
Is that a teapot? Who throws a teapot in a river?
The water's clearing already. I can see the stones.

Some of it's out. Not enough, but some.

{client} says the water's running clear under the bridge. Good work.
A corked bottle with a letter inside, addressed to {addressee}. Here, in the village.

Good. Rakes by the shed. Pick one with all its teeth.

No? Then the paths stay slippery for another week.

Lovely work. The Academy teachers will think it's a different park.

Snow still on half the roofs. We'll keep an ear on the beams tonight.
